title: A Theoretical Analysis of the Test Error of Finite-Rank Kernel Ridge Regression

en.text: Here is a recipe you have almost certainly used: take a pretrained network, freeze the backbone, and retrain only the final linear layer. It is fast, cheap, and everywhere — from few-shot transfer to reservoir computing. What is less obvious is that this recipe is exactly kernel ridge regression (KRR) with a finite-rank kernel. The frozen features define a fixed, finite-dimensional feature map, and fitting the last layer is ridge regression in that feature space, whose kernel has rank equal to the number of frozen features it exposes.

A natural question follows: how large is the test error of that last layer, and can we certify it before ever touching the test set? Statistical learning theory has answers for KRR in general, but in the finite-rank regime those answers are loose. Classical bounds are frequently one-sided (upper bounds only), several require the ridge parameter λ to stay bounded away from zero, and some become vacuous precisely in the ridgeless limit λ→0 that last-layer training tends to approach. Without a matching lower bound, you also cannot tell whether a small upper bound is genuinely small or merely optimistic.

This NeurIPS 2023 paper closes the gap. For finite-rank KRR in the under-parameterized regime — sample size N larger than the kernel rank M — the authors derive matching non-asymptotic, high-probability upper and lower bounds on the test error. The bounds stay tight for any ridge λ, including the ridgeless limit, and empirically the new upper bound tracks the true error where the closest prior bound floats orders of magnitude above it.

en.caption: Figure 1. Finite-rank KRR on a truncated neural tangent kernel (tNTK). Left: with N=50 samples and rank M=7, the regressor (green) tracks the target (blue) despite noisy samples (red). Right: median test error over 10 trials drops steeply as N grows from 10 to 200 (shaded interquartile bands).

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00987 (NeurIPS 2023). Authors: Tin Sum Cheng, Aurelien Lucchi, Ivan Dokmanić, Anastasis Kratsios, and David Belius.
Why the finite-rank regime breaks the textbook bounds

A finite-rank kernel spans a finite-dimensional space inside the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), with an eigenbasis of M functions. The target the model must learn rarely lives entirely in that span. It splits into an in-span part, which finite-rank KRR can in principle recover, and an orthogonal complement that the estimator can never represent. That complement is an irreducible finite-rank error: a floor on the test error that no amount of extra data removes, and a term the analysis has to track honestly rather than wish away.

Prior finite-rank analyses each miss part of this picture. Some hold only in asymptotic, high-dimensional limits; others are valid only when λ decays on a prescribed schedule tied to the sample size N; others bound only the expected error rather than a single realized run; and almost none supply a lower bound. A one-sided, asymptotic, schedule-dependent guarantee is not what you want when you have one frozen backbone, one dataset, and one value of λ in front of you.
A bias–variance split, analyzed in the eigenfunction basis
The starting point is the ordinary KRR estimator — the minimizer of a regularized least-squares objective over the RKHS:
f_{Z,λ} = argmin_{f∈H}  (1/N) Σᵢ (f(xᵢ) − yᵢ)² + λ‖f‖²_H.

The test error is the expected squared deviation from the true target, and it splits cleanly into a bias term (the error with noiseless labels) and a variance term (driven by label noise). The authors bound each piece separately, with high probability. The move that makes the constants sharp is a change of coordinates: instead of working in the RKHS basis, they analyze the target in the L²ρ eigenfunction basis {ψk}. This decouples the kernel spectrum from the randomness of where the samples happen to land, which is precisely the coupling that inflates earlier bounds.

Two technical ingredients carry the proof: a sub-Gaussian concentration result for the random covariance matrix, and a Neumann-series expansion of the matrix inverse that appears in the ridge terms. Together they let the bound hold for any λ chosen independently of N — not just for a ridge that must shrink as the sample grows. Concretely, the variance obeys a bound of the form
variance ≤ σ² · (2M/N) · (1 + √(log N / N)) + C₂ · (log N / N),

so it scales like the noise variance times twice the rank over the sample size, with residue terms that fade at a log N / N rate. That decay is an order of magnitude faster than the O(√(log N / N)) rate a generic Rademacher-complexity argument would deliver here.
The payoff: bounds that actually bracket the error

The most visible gain is against the closest prior result, due to Bach. The figure below plots both upper bounds on a natural-log scale, once as the sample size N varies and once as the inverse ridge 1/λ varies. The new bound sits far below Bach's across the board, and — crucially — it keeps improving toward the ridgeless direction (large 1/λ) where Bach's bound turns around and gets worse. That contrast isolates the ridge dependence as the main source of the improvement.

en.caption: Figure 2. New upper bound (green) vs Bach's upper bound (blue) on the tNTK, natural-log scale. Left: varying N. Right: varying inverse ridge 1/λ. The new bound is orders of magnitude lower and keeps improving as regularization vanishes, where Bach's turns worse.

en.text: A lower bound is what turns a good upper bound into a tight one. The next figure overlays the paper's upper and lower bounds (with the small residue terms dropped for clarity) on the measured test error for two controlled finite-rank kernels — the tNTK and a separately constructed low-rank kernel (LK). The two bounds sandwich the median error across the range of N and squeeze together as N grows, which is the empirical signature of tightness. Because the residues are omitted, the simplified bounds stop bracketing the error at very small N, exactly where the theory says those terms still matter; they recover their grip as the sample grows and the small residues steadily fade away.

en.caption: Figure 3. Upper and lower bounds (residues dropped) vs measured test error over 10 trials, on the tNTK (left) and low-rank kernel LK (right), natural-log scale. The bounds bracket the median error and converge as N grows; the small-N gap is expected.

Yes, any λ independent of N

en.text: What it means, and where it stops

The practical reading is that finite-rank KRR — the model behind last-layer fine-tuning — now comes with an honest, two-sided certificate of its test error. The bounds hold with high probability (at least 1 − 2/N over the random sampling), they stay tight for any ridge including none at all, and they make the irreducible finite-rank floor explicit rather than hiding it. The enabling idea — analyze the target in the eigenfunction basis to separate spectrum from sampling noise — is a template other finite-rank analyses can borrow.

The honest boundary: the results are for the under-parameterized regime where N exceeds the rank M, and the validation uses controlled synthetic kernels (tNTK and LK) where the spectrum and target decomposition are known, not natural-image datasets. In the ridgeless limit the analysis further shows the bias is governed purely by the finite-rank error and the variance purely by the noise level σ². Within those limits, this is a much sharper certificate than the loose, one-sided, asymptotic guarantees that came before.

zh.text: 有一种做法你几乎一定用过：拿一个预训练网络，冻住主干，只重新训练最后一层线性层。它快、省、而且到处都是，从少样本迁移到 reservoir computing 都在用。不那么显然的是，这个做法本质上就是一次有限秩核（finite-rank kernel）上的核岭回归（KRR）。冻住的特征定义了一个固定的、有限维的特征映射，训练最后一层就是在这个特征空间里做岭回归，其核的秩正好等于特征的个数。

一个自然的问题随之而来：这最后一层的测试误差有多大？我们能不能在还没碰测试集之前就给它一个可信的保证？统计学习理论对一般的 KRR 是有答案的，但落到有限秩这个具体场景，这些答案往往很松。经典的界通常是单向的（只有上界），不少要求岭参数 λ 不能太靠近零，还有一些恰好在最后一层训练最想接近的无正则极限 λ→0 处变得平凡（vacuous）。更麻烦的是，没有一个匹配的下界，你就无法判断一个看起来很小的上界究竟是真的小，还是只是过于乐观。
这篇 NeurIPS 2023 的工作补上了这个缺口。针对欠参数化区间（样本量 N 大于核的秩 M）下的有限秩 KRR，作者推出了相互匹配的、非渐近的高概率上界与下界。这组界对任意岭参数 λ 都保持紧致，包括 ridgeless 极限；而在实验中，新的上界能贴着真实误差走，而此前最接近的界却高出它一个数量级以上。

zh.caption: 图1 有限秩 KRR 在截断神经正切核（tNTK）上的表现。左：在 N=50 个样本、核秩 M=7 下，回归器（绿）尽管面对含噪样本（红）仍紧贴目标函数（蓝）。右：测试误差中位数（10 次重复）随 N 从 10 增长到 200 迅速下降，阴影为四分位带。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00987 （NeurIPS 2023）。作者：Tin Sum Cheng、Aurelien Lucchi、Ivan Dokmanić、Anastasis Kratsios、David Belius。
为什么有限秩场景会让教科书里的界失灵
一个有限秩核在再生核希尔伯特空间（RKHS）里只张成一个有限维子空间，对应 M 个特征函数构成的特征基。而模型要学的目标函数，几乎从不完全落在这个子空间里。它会分成两部分：一部分落在子空间内，有限秩 KRR 原则上可以复原；另一部分正交于子空间，估计器永远无法表示。后者就是不可约的有限秩误差：一层再多数据也抹不掉的测试误差下限，也是分析里必须老老实实追踪、而不能一笔带过的项。
以往的有限秩分析各自漏掉了这幅图的一块。有的只在渐近的高维极限下成立；有的只有当 λ 按一个与样本量 N 绑定的时间表衰减时才有效；有的只界住期望误差，而不是某一次真实运行的误差；几乎没有谁给出下界。当你手上只有一个冻住的主干、一份数据、一个 λ 取值时，一个单向的、渐近的、依赖衰减时间表的保证并不是你想要的东西。
偏差—方差分解，放到特征函数基里去做
出发点是普通的 KRR 估计器，也就是在 RKHS 上最小化一个带正则的最小二乘目标：
f_{Z,λ} = argmin_{f∈H}  (1/N) Σᵢ (f(xᵢ) − yᵢ)² + λ‖f‖²_H。
测试误差被定义为与真实目标的期望平方偏差，它干净地分成一个偏差项（无噪标签下的误差）和一个方差项（由标签噪声驱动）。作者对这两块分别给出高概率的界。真正让常数变紧的一步是换坐标：不在 RKHS 基里做，而是把目标放到 L²ρ 特征函数基 {ψk} 里分析。这样就把核的谱和「样本恰好落在哪里」的随机性解耦开来，而正是这种耦合把以往的界撑松了。
证明由两个技术要件支撑：一个针对随机协方差矩阵的 sub-Gaussian 集中不等式，以及对岭项里出现的矩阵逆的 Neumann 级数展开。二者合在一起，让界对任意与 N 无关地选取的 λ 都成立，而不只是对必须随样本增大而衰减的岭参数成立。具体地，方差满足如下形式的界：
variance ≤ σ² · (2M/N) · (1 + √(log N / N)) + C₂ · (log N / N)，
也就是说，它按「噪声方差乘以两倍的秩再除以样本量」的量级增长，残差项以 log N / N 的速率淡出。这个衰减速率，比一般 Rademacher 复杂度论证给出的 O(√(log N / N)) 速率快了一个数量级。
回报：真正把误差夹在中间的界
最直观的收益来自与最接近的前人结果（Bach 的界）的对比。下图在自然对数尺度下画出两个上界，一次让样本量 N 变化，一次让岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新的界全程都远在 Bach 的界之下，而且更关键的是，它在朝 ridgeless 方向（1/λ 增大）时还在持续变好，而 Bach 的界却在这里掉头变差。这个对比把改进的主要来源锁定在了对岭的依赖上。

zh.caption: 图2 新上界（绿）与 Bach 上界（蓝）在 tNTK 上的对比，自然对数尺度。左：随 N 变化；右：随岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新界低出若干数量级，且正则越弱越好，而 Bach 的界在此掉头变差。

zh.text: 把一个好的上界变成一个紧的界，靠的是下界。下图把论文的上界和下界（为清楚起见略去了小的残差项）叠在两个受控有限秩核的实测测试误差上——一个是 tNTK，一个是单独构造的低秩核（LK）。两条界在整个 N 的范围内把误差中位数夹在中间，并随 N 增大彼此收拢，这正是「紧」在实验上的标志。由于略去了残差，简化后的界在 N 很小时不再夹住误差，恰好落在理论所说、这些项仍然重要的地方；当样本增大、残差淡出后，界又重新夹住了误差。

zh.caption: 图3 上界与下界（略去残差）对实测测试误差（10 次重复）的对比，左为 tNTK、右为低秩核 LK，自然对数尺度。两条界夹住误差中位数并随 N 增大收拢；小 N 处的缝隙在预期之内。

zh.text: 一览：新分析补了什么

zh.caption: 表1 新分析相比以往有限秩 KRR 界的增量。
rows: 有，且随 N 增大与上界匹配
是，任意与 N 无关的 λ

zh.text: 它意味着什么，又止步于哪里
从实践角度读，有限秩 KRR——也就是最后一层微调背后的模型——如今有了一份诚实的、双向的测试误差证书。这些界以高概率成立（对随机采样至少 1 − 2/N），对任意岭都保持紧致，哪怕完全无正则；它还把不可约的有限秩误差下限显式地摆出来，而不是藏起来。而使这一切成立的核心想法——在特征函数基里分析目标、把谱和采样噪声分开——是一个其他有限秩分析也能借用的模板。
诚实地划出边界：这些结果针对的是 N 超过秩 M 的欠参数化区间，验证用的是谱和目标分解都已知的受控合成核（tNTK 与 LK），而非自然图像数据集。在 ridgeless 极限下，分析进一步表明偏差完全由有限秩误差主导、方差完全由噪声水平 σ² 主导。在这些限定之内，这是一份远比此前那些松散、单向、渐近的保证都更锐利的证书。

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 给「只训练最后一层」一个真正紧的泛化保证
zh.subtitle: 巴塞尔大学等提出有限秩核岭回归（finite-rank KRR）测试误差的双向非渐近界：对任意正则强度都保持紧致，包括无正则的 ridgeless 极限。

en.caption: Figure 1. Finite-rank KRR on a truncated neural tangent kernel (tNTK). Left: with N=50 samples and rank M=7, the regressor (green) tracks the target (blue) despite noisy samples (red). Right: median test error over 10 trials drops steeply as N grows from 10 to 200 (shaded interquartile bands).

en.text: Why the finite-rank regime breaks the textbook bounds

A finite-rank kernel spans a finite-dimensional space inside the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), with an eigenbasis of M functions. The target the model must learn rarely lives entirely in that span. It splits into an in-span part, which finite-rank KRR can in principle recover, and an orthogonal complement that the estimator can never represent. That complement is an irreducible finite-rank error: a floor on the test error that no amount of extra data removes, and a term the analysis has to track honestly rather than wish away.

Prior finite-rank analyses each miss part of this picture. Some hold only in asymptotic, high-dimensional limits; others are valid only when λ decays on a prescribed schedule tied to the sample size N; others bound only the expected error rather than a single realized run; and almost none supply a lower bound. A one-sided, asymptotic, schedule-dependent guarantee is not what you want when you have one frozen backbone, one dataset, and one value of λ in front of you.

zh.caption: 图1 有限秩 KRR 在截断神经正切核（tNTK）上的表现。左：在 N=50 个样本、核秩 M=7 下，回归器（绿）尽管面对含噪样本（红）仍紧贴目标函数（蓝）。右：测试误差中位数（10 次重复）随 N 从 10 增长到 200 迅速下降，阴影为四分位带。

zh.text: 偏差—方差分解，放到特征函数基里去做
出发点是普通的 KRR 估计器，也就是在 RKHS 上最小化一个带正则的最小二乘目标：
f_{Z,λ} = argmin_{f∈H}  (1/N) Σᵢ (f(xᵢ) − yᵢ)² + λ‖f‖²_H。
测试误差被定义为与真实目标的期望平方偏差，它干净地分成一个偏差项（无噪标签下的误差）和一个方差项（由标签噪声驱动）。作者对这两块分别给出高概率的界。真正让常数变紧的一步是换坐标：不在 RKHS 基里做，而是把目标放到 L²ρ 特征函数基 {ψk} 里分析。这样就把核的谱和「样本恰好落在哪里」的随机性解耦开来，而正是这种耦合把以往的界撑松了。
证明由两个技术要件支撑：一个针对随机协方差矩阵的 sub-Gaussian 集中不等式，以及对岭项里出现的矩阵逆的 Neumann 级数展开。二者合在一起，让界对任意与 N 无关地选取的 λ 都成立，而不只是对必须随样本增大而衰减的岭参数成立。具体地，方差满足如下形式的界：
variance ≤ σ² · (2M/N) · (1 + √(log N / N)) + C₂ · (log N / N)，
也就是说，它按「噪声方差乘以两倍的秩再除以样本量」的量级增长，残差项以 log N / N 的速率淡出。这个衰减速率，比一般 Rademacher 复杂度论证给出的 O(√(log N / N)) 速率快了一个数量级。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: A Sharp, Two-Sided Test-Error Bound for Finite-Rank KRR
en.subtitle: Freeze a pretrained network, retrain only its last layer, and you are doing finite-rank kernel ridge regression — a regime where the textbook generalization bounds go loose. This paper makes them tight in both directions, for any amount of regularization.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 给「只训练最后一层」一个真正紧的泛化保证
zh.subtitle: 巴塞尔大学等提出有限秩核岭回归（finite-rank KRR）测试误差的双向非渐近界：对任意正则强度都保持紧致，包括无正则的 ridgeless 极限。

en.caption: Figure 1. Finite-rank KRR on a truncated neural tangent kernel (tNTK). Left: with N=50 samples and rank M=7, the regressor (green) tracks the target (blue) despite noisy samples (red). Right: median test error over 10 trials drops steeply as N grows from 10 to 200 (shaded interquartile bands).

en.text: What it means, and where it stops

The practical reading is that finite-rank KRR — the model behind last-layer fine-tuning — now comes with an honest, two-sided certificate of its test error. The bounds hold with high probability (at least 1 − 2/N over the random sampling), they stay tight for any ridge including none at all, and they make the irreducible finite-rank floor explicit rather than hiding it. The enabling idea — analyze the target in the eigenfunction basis to separate spectrum from sampling noise — is a template other finite-rank analyses can borrow.

The honest boundary: the results are for the under-parameterized regime where N exceeds the rank M, and the validation uses controlled synthetic kernels (tNTK and LK) where the spectrum and target decomposition are known, not natural-image datasets. In the ridgeless limit the analysis further shows the bias is governed purely by the finite-rank error and the variance purely by the noise level σ². Within those limits, this is a much sharper certificate than the loose, one-sided, asymptotic guarantees that came before.

zh.text: 回报：真正把误差夹在中间的界
最直观的收益来自与最接近的前人结果（Bach 的界）的对比。下图在自然对数尺度下画出两个上界，一次让样本量 N 变化，一次让岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新的界全程都远在 Bach 的界之下，而且更关键的是，它在朝 ridgeless 方向（1/λ 增大）时还在持续变好，而 Bach 的界却在这里掉头变差。这个对比把改进的主要来源锁定在了对岭的依赖上。

zh.caption: 图2 新上界（绿）与 Bach 上界（蓝）在 tNTK 上的对比，自然对数尺度。左：随 N 变化；右：随岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新界低出若干数量级，且正则越弱越好，而 Bach 的界在此掉头变差。

zh.text: 把一个好的上界变成一个紧的界，靠的是下界。下图把论文的上界和下界（为清楚起见略去了小的残差项）叠在两个受控有限秩核的实测测试误差上——一个是 tNTK，一个是单独构造的低秩核（LK）。两条界在整个 N 的范围内把误差中位数夹在中间，并随 N 增大彼此收拢，这正是「紧」在实验上的标志。由于略去了残差，简化后的界在 N 很小时不再夹住误差，恰好落在理论所说、这些项仍然重要的地方；当样本增大、残差淡出后，界又重新夹住了误差。

zh.caption: 图3 上界与下界（略去残差）对实测测试误差（10 次重复）的对比，左为 tNTK、右为低秩核 LK，自然对数尺度。两条界夹住误差中位数并随 N 增大收拢；小 N 处的缝隙在预期之内。

zh.subtitle: 巴塞尔大学等提出有限秩核岭回归（finite-rank KRR）测试误差的双向非渐近界：对任意正则强度都保持紧致，包括无正则的 ridgeless 极限。

en.caption: Figure 1. Finite-rank KRR on a truncated neural tangent kernel (tNTK). Left: with N=50 samples and rank M=7, the regressor (green) tracks the target (blue) despite noisy samples (red). Right: median test error over 10 trials drops steeply as N grows from 10 to 200 (shaded interquartile bands).

en.text: Why the finite-rank regime breaks the textbook bounds

A finite-rank kernel spans a finite-dimensional space inside the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), with an eigenbasis of M functions. The target the model must learn rarely lives entirely in that span. It splits into an in-span part, which finite-rank KRR can in principle recover, and an orthogonal complement that the estimator can never represent. That complement is an irreducible finite-rank error: a floor on the test error that no amount of extra data removes, and a term the analysis has to track honestly rather than wish away.

Prior finite-rank analyses each miss part of this picture. Some hold only in asymptotic, high-dimensional limits; others are valid only when λ decays on a prescribed schedule tied to the sample size N; others bound only the expected error rather than a single realized run; and almost none supply a lower bound. A one-sided, asymptotic, schedule-dependent guarantee is not what you want when you have one frozen backbone, one dataset, and one value of λ in front of you.

zh.text: 有一种做法你几乎一定用过：拿一个预训练网络，冻住主干，只重新训练最后一层线性层。它快、省、而且到处都是，从少样本迁移到 reservoir computing 都在用。不那么显然的是，这个做法本质上就是一次有限秩核（finite-rank kernel）上的核岭回归（KRR）。冻住的特征定义了一个固定的、有限维的特征映射，训练最后一层就是在这个特征空间里做岭回归，其核的秩正好等于特征的个数。

一个自然的问题随之而来：这最后一层的测试误差有多大？我们能不能在还没碰测试集之前就给它一个可信的保证？统计学习理论对一般的 KRR 是有答案的，但落到有限秩这个具体场景，这些答案往往很松。经典的界通常是单向的（只有上界），不少要求岭参数 λ 不能太靠近零，还有一些恰好在最后一层训练最想接近的无正则极限 λ→0 处变得平凡（vacuous）。更麻烦的是，没有一个匹配的下界，你就无法判断一个看起来很小的上界究竟是真的小，还是只是过于乐观。
这篇 NeurIPS 2023 的工作补上了这个缺口。针对欠参数化区间（样本量 N 大于核的秩 M）下的有限秩 KRR，作者推出了相互匹配的、非渐近的高概率上界与下界。这组界对任意岭参数 λ 都保持紧致，包括 ridgeless 极限；而在实验中，新的上界能贴着真实误差走，而此前最接近的界却高出它一个数量级以上。

zh.caption: 图1 有限秩 KRR 在截断神经正切核（tNTK）上的表现。左：在 N=50 个样本、核秩 M=7 下，回归器（绿）尽管面对含噪样本（红）仍紧贴目标函数（蓝）。右：测试误差中位数（10 次重复）随 N 从 10 增长到 200 迅速下降，阴影为四分位带。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00987 （NeurIPS 2023）。作者：Tin Sum Cheng、Aurelien Lucchi、Ivan Dokmanić、Anastasis Kratsios、David Belius。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023: A Sharp, Two-Sided Test-Error Bound for Finite-Rank KRR
en.subtitle: Freeze a pretrained network, retrain only its last layer, and you are doing finite-rank kernel ridge regression — a regime where the textbook generalization bounds go loose. This paper makes them tight in both directions, for any amount of regularization.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 给「只训练最后一层」一个真正紧的泛化保证
zh.subtitle: 巴塞尔大学等提出有限秩核岭回归（finite-rank KRR）测试误差的双向非渐近界：对任意正则强度都保持紧致，包括无正则的 ridgeless 极限。

en.text: A bias–variance split, analyzed in the eigenfunction basis
The starting point is the ordinary KRR estimator — the minimizer of a regularized least-squares objective over the RKHS:
f_{Z,λ} = argmin_{f∈H}  (1/N) Σᵢ (f(xᵢ) − yᵢ)² + λ‖f‖²_H.

The test error is the expected squared deviation from the true target, and it splits cleanly into a bias term (the error with noiseless labels) and a variance term (driven by label noise). The authors bound each piece separately, with high probability. The move that makes the constants sharp is a change of coordinates: instead of working in the RKHS basis, they analyze the target in the L²ρ eigenfunction basis {ψk}. This decouples the kernel spectrum from the randomness of where the samples happen to land, which is precisely the coupling that inflates earlier bounds.

Two technical ingredients carry the proof: a sub-Gaussian concentration result for the random covariance matrix, and a Neumann-series expansion of the matrix inverse that appears in the ridge terms. Together they let the bound hold for any λ chosen independently of N — not just for a ridge that must shrink as the sample grows. Concretely, the variance obeys a bound of the form
variance ≤ σ² · (2M/N) · (1 + √(log N / N)) + C₂ · (log N / N),

so it scales like the noise variance times twice the rank over the sample size, with residue terms that fade at a log N / N rate. That decay is an order of magnitude faster than the O(√(log N / N)) rate a generic Rademacher-complexity argument would deliver here.
The payoff: bounds that actually bracket the error

The most visible gain is against the closest prior result, due to Bach. The figure below plots both upper bounds on a natural-log scale, once as the sample size N varies and once as the inverse ridge 1/λ varies. The new bound sits far below Bach's across the board, and — crucially — it keeps improving toward the ridgeless direction (large 1/λ) where Bach's bound turns around and gets worse. That contrast isolates the ridge dependence as the main source of the improvement.

en.caption: Figure 2. New upper bound (green) vs Bach's upper bound (blue) on the tNTK, natural-log scale. Left: varying N. Right: varying inverse ridge 1/λ. The new bound is orders of magnitude lower and keeps improving as regularization vanishes, where Bach's turns worse.

en.text: A lower bound is what turns a good upper bound into a tight one. The next figure overlays the paper's upper and lower bounds (with the small residue terms dropped for clarity) on the measured test error for two controlled finite-rank kernels — the tNTK and a separately constructed low-rank kernel (LK). The two bounds sandwich the median error across the range of N and squeeze together as N grows, which is the empirical signature of tightness. Because the residues are omitted, the simplified bounds stop bracketing the error at very small N, exactly where the theory says those terms still matter; they recover their grip as the sample grows and the small residues steadily fade away.

en.caption: Figure 3. Upper and lower bounds (residues dropped) vs measured test error over 10 trials, on the tNTK (left) and low-rank kernel LK (right), natural-log scale. The bounds bracket the median error and converge as N grows; the small-N gap is expected.

zh.text: 回报：真正把误差夹在中间的界
最直观的收益来自与最接近的前人结果（Bach 的界）的对比。下图在自然对数尺度下画出两个上界，一次让样本量 N 变化，一次让岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新的界全程都远在 Bach 的界之下，而且更关键的是，它在朝 ridgeless 方向（1/λ 增大）时还在持续变好，而 Bach 的界却在这里掉头变差。这个对比把改进的主要来源锁定在了对岭的依赖上。

zh.caption: 图2 新上界（绿）与 Bach 上界（蓝）在 tNTK 上的对比，自然对数尺度。左：随 N 变化；右：随岭的倒数 1/λ 变化。新界低出若干数量级，且正则越弱越好，而 Bach 的界在此掉头变差。

zh.text: 把一个好的上界变成一个紧的界，靠的是下界。下图把论文的上界和下界（为清楚起见略去了小的残差项）叠在两个受控有限秩核的实测测试误差上——一个是 tNTK，一个是单独构造的低秩核（LK）。两条界在整个 N 的范围内把误差中位数夹在中间，并随 N 增大彼此收拢，这正是「紧」在实验上的标志。由于略去了残差，简化后的界在 N 很小时不再夹住误差，恰好落在理论所说、这些项仍然重要的地方；当样本增大、残差淡出后，界又重新夹住了误差。

zh.caption: 图3 上界与下界（略去残差）对实测测试误差（10 次重复）的对比，左为 tNTK、右为低秩核 LK，自然对数尺度。两条界夹住误差中位数并随 N 增大收拢；小 N 处的缝隙在预期之内。

zh.text: 它意味着什么，又止步于哪里
从实践角度读，有限秩 KRR——也就是最后一层微调背后的模型——如今有了一份诚实的、双向的测试误差证书。这些界以高概率成立（对随机采样至少 1 − 2/N），对任意岭都保持紧致，哪怕完全无正则；它还把不可约的有限秩误差下限显式地摆出来，而不是藏起来。而使这一切成立的核心想法——在特征函数基里分析目标、把谱和采样噪声分开——是一个其他有限秩分析也能借用的模板。
诚实地划出边界：这些结果针对的是 N 超过秩 M 的欠参数化区间，验证用的是谱和目标分解都已知的受控合成核（tNTK 与 LK），而非自然图像数据集。在 ridgeless 极限下，分析进一步表明偏差完全由有限秩误差主导、方差完全由噪声水平 σ² 主导。在这些限定之内，这是一份远比此前那些松散、单向、渐近的保证都更锐利的证书。

诚实地划出边界：这些结果针对的是 N 超过秩 M 的欠参数化区间，验证用的是谱和目标分解都已知的受控合成核（tNTK 与 LK），而非自然图像数据集。在 ridgeless 极限下，分析进一步表明偏差完全由有限秩误差主导、方差完全由噪声水平 σ² 主导。在这些限定之内，这是一份远比此前那些松散、单向、渐近的保证都更锐利的证书。

en.caption: Figure 1. Finite-rank KRR on a truncated neural tangent kernel (tNTK). Left: with N=50 samples and rank M=7, the regressor (green) tracks the target (blue) despite noisy samples (red). Right: median test error over 10 trials drops steeply as N grows from 10 to 200 (shaded interquartile bands).

en.text: What it means, and where it stops

The practical reading is that finite-rank KRR — the model behind last-layer fine-tuning — now comes with an honest, two-sided certificate of its test error. The bounds hold with high probability (at least 1 − 2/N over the random sampling), they stay tight for any ridge including none at all, and they make the irreducible finite-rank floor explicit rather than hiding it. The enabling idea — analyze the target in the eigenfunction basis to separate spectrum from sampling noise — is a template other finite-rank analyses can borrow.

The honest boundary: the results are for the under-parameterized regime where N exceeds the rank M, and the validation uses controlled synthetic kernels (tNTK and LK) where the spectrum and target decomposition are known, not natural-image datasets. In the ridgeless limit the analysis further shows the bias is governed purely by the finite-rank error and the variance purely by the noise level σ². Within those limits, this is a much sharper certificate than the loose, one-sided, asymptotic guarantees that came before.
